card.name: Sentence-opening instruction verbs in labels
card.fires_on: The first word of an instruction sentence in a drug label, mostly Refer, Monitor or Begin, right after the previous sentence ends. It is strongest when the sentence tells the reader to look elsewhere or to check something.

modes.label: Refer to another document
modes.description: The word Refer or refer starts a pointer to guidelines, prescribing information or a package insert.
modes.example: << Refer>> to your Institution’s guidelines and all applicable

modes.label: Monitor or begin directive
modes.description: Monitor or Begin opens a sentence giving a clinical action instruction.

modes.label: Other sentence-ending nouns
modes.description: Occasionally a noun such as surveillance or studies just before an instruction or finding.
modes.example: In animal<< studies>>, embryo-fetal developmental toxicity was shown

card.writes: It pushes toward code-like or abbreviation tokens such as CFR and ATS and away from some Chinese words, so there is no clear link to the text pattern.
card.plain: It lights up on the verb that starts an instruction sentence, like Refer to or Monitor, in a drug label.
